title: Seal-in in Ladder: a motor that holds itself on
summary: Edit a Ladder rung so that a Start press keeps the motor on after the button is released, and a Stop press drops it even while Start is still pressed.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real stop button or motor starter is wired.
objectives: Read a Ladder rung as a path of contacts that must all pass power to reach a coil.
Make a coil hold itself on after Start is released, in a rung where Stop always wins over Start.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/SealIn.ld.json one rung is drawn: a normally closed contact on StopPB, a normally open contact on StartPB and the coil Motor. The motor runs only while Start is held. Make the motor keep running once started, until Stop is pressed, and make Stop win when both buttons are pressed together.
stages.checkpoint: You can say what must stay TRUE for the motor to keep running after Start is released, and what must always be able to stop it.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict Motor at {{t:30}} ms (Start was released at {{t:20}} ms), at {{t:50}} ms (Stop was released) and at {{t:70}} ms (Start and Stop pressed together).
stages.checkpoint: {{v:SealIn.Motor=true@30|ON}} at {{t:30}} ms; {{v:SealIn.Motor=false@50|OFF}} at {{t:50}} ms, because nobody is pressing Start; {{v:SealIn.Motor=false@70|OFF}} at {{t:70}} ms, because Stop wins.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program drives Motor only while StartPB is pressed, so it drops out as soon as Start is released at {{t:20}} ms. Change it so that Motor stays ON after Start is released, turns OFF when Stop is pressed at {{t:40}} ms, stays OFF when Stop is released, and stays OFF at {{t:70}} ms when Start and Stop are pressed together.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named SealIn and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:20}}, {{t:30}} and {{t:40}} ms: Motor stays ON at {{t:30}} ms with Start released, and drops at {{t:40}} ms when Stop is pressed.
stages.checkpoint: Motor rises once at {{t:10}} ms and falls once at {{t:40}} ms; it does not start again at {{t:50}} ms when Stop is released.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: At {{t:70}} ms Start and Stop are pressed together. Which assertion covers that moment, and which contact of your rung keeps the motor OFF then?
stages.checkpoint: You can follow the power through your rung at {{t:70}} ms and say which contact stops it, and which assertion would fail if that contact did not stop it.

hints.text: Look at what is still TRUE in the scan after Start is released while the motor runs, and at which contact every path to the coil must pass.
Add a normally open contact on Motor in the second row, under the StartPB contact, and join it to the first row so the two are in parallel. Leave the StopPB contact where it is.

faultCases: The starting program drives Motor only while StartPB is pressed, so it drops out as soon as Start is released at {{t:20}} ms.
